blocks.text: Intro to electrical engineering and DC circuits
Introduction to electrical engineering and D C circuits
An electric circuit consists of a closed path interconnecting active and passive elements.
The components are called circuit elements.
A closed path followed by direct current (DC) is called a DC circuit.
A closed path followed by alternating current (AC) is called an AC circuit.
The source supplies electrical energy to the load, which converts it into heat or other forms of energy. In a DC circuit, loads may be connected in series, parallel or series-parallel.

blocks.text: Charge is a characteristic property associated with particles of matter such as protons, neutrons and electrons.
Protons have positive charge, electrons have negative charge and neutrons are neutral.
The unit of charge is coulomb (C)
A steady current can be represented as \(I=\dfrac{Q}{T}\), where \(Q=\text{charge}\) and \(T=\text{time}\).
A time varying current can be expressed as \(i=\dfrac{dq}{dt}\).
Current is the rate of flow of charge through the cross-sectional area of a conductor.
Absolute potential is the work required to move a unit positive test charge from infinity to a point in the field.
Potential difference is the work required to move a unit positive test charge from one point to another in the field.
Energy is the capacity to do work. It may exist in forms such as electrical, mechanical and thermal energy.
Power is the rate at which electrical energy is converted into other forms of energy. It is the product of voltage and current.
